items.title: George Blanchin Interview, 1959-11-13
items.q: And Johnny Tobin had a band at that time, I think, at the ringside, and he cut the other side of the record, as you recall.

ctx.x: Black Eagle Vels there. You don't remember them? Those are people George Lewis has mentioned to me, playing over there. Who are some of the people you heard here in town?

Well, I was going to say, just about that time in New Orleans, of course this was, I suppose, the golden era of jazz around this part of the country, because in New Orleans around that time you had bands like, well, of course you had P-Ron out of Tranchina's. You had the old Chris Kelly and the Tuxedo bands, Celestan's band, playing for dancers. You had the Halfway House Band, out of Chris Rabinstein's Halfway House. Well, shortly after that, the Owls at the West End Roof, and the Owls also at the Pontchartrain…
I have heard of them. I think it was Pinky.
